stories.headline: US consumer prices rise 0.4% in October, above forecasts; Fed's Waller backs December rate hike
stories.summary: US consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, against an expected 0.3%. Core prices rose 0.3%, against an expected 0.2%. Before the data came out, Fed Governor Christopher Waller said he would support a quarter-point rate rise at the December 8-9 meeting, and that a half-point rise should be considered if core inflation came in at about 0.3%. Nasdaq-100 futures fell about 1% after the report, and futures pricing put the chance of a December hike near 97%.

stories.headline: Volatility index posts its largest one-day drop of 2026 as stocks rebound
stories.summary: The Cboe VIX fell about 22% on Monday to 19.92. That was its largest one-day decline of the year and took it back under 20, two sessions after it closed above 28 following last week's sell-off. The S&P 500 rose 2.35%, its best day since April, and the Russell 2000 gained more than 3%.

stories.headline: Anthropic sets IPO price range as investors weigh AI spending
stories.summary: Anthropic released a price range on Tuesday for its planned Nasdaq listing under the ticker ANT. The IPO is expected to be one of the largest on record. An amended filing showed about $895 billion in computing commitments and a third-quarter operating loss of $567 million. The news comes days after Nasdaq-100 stocks fell sharply over worries about AI data-center spending and then partly recovered.

stories.headline: Digital Turbine shares fall about 23% as profit outlook holds flat despite revenue beat
stories.summary: Digital Turbine shares fell about 23% in morning trading on Tuesday. The company beat revenue estimates and raised its sales forecast, but it kept its adjusted EBITDA forecast unchanged, reported a lower gross margin and revised costs it had understated. Before the drop, the stock was up about 75% this year.

stories.headline: US stocks rise for a second day, recovering more of last week's post-election losses as oil falls
stories.summary: The S&P 500 rose about 2% and the Nasdaq more than 2% on Monday. Stocks have now gained for two days in a row after last week's sell-off, which was driven by fears that Democratic midterm wins could slow the building of AI data centers. Lower oil prices helped, and the Dow moved back above its Election Day close.

stories.headline: Oil extends slide on hopes for US-Iran talks after Brent's worst week since 2020
stories.summary: Brent crude fell about 4% to 5%, to near $94 a barrel, and WTI fell to around $87. The drop came after President Trump said renewed US strikes on Iran were highly unlikely while diplomacy continues. Brent fell 16% last week, its sharpest weekly drop since the start of the COVID-19 pandemic, and is down from more than $112 at the start of the month. Shares of companies with large fuel bills led gains.

stories.headline: Nvidia shares fall about 5% after board opens probe into CEO Jensen Huang
stories.summary: Nvidia's board started an independent investigation after reports that CEO Jensen Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort through a relationship with a businesswoman whom US agencies call a Chinese spy. Huang admitted to an affair and said he would cooperate with the review. Shares fell about 4% to 5%, wiping out more than $200 billion in market value, while other chip stocks rose.
